## 2026-11-13 - Talos's Library: dragging the view works (and keeps working over the interface)
Asked: "panning views in libraries is very laggy and sometimes it does not seem to handle drag and drop event well".

Found:
- Inside Talos, a drag on the Library's view didn't reach it at all. Talos's host screen (editor_screen.gd) is a full-screen Control with the default mouse filter (STOP). The Library is a world (Node2D) under it, so the host swallowed every press and motion meant for the view. Measured with simulated input: 0 px of pan for a 540 px drag (the Library opened on its own: 540 px).
- The drag was also fragile. It used one flag for any button, panned only on motion the interface didn't take, and ended only on a release that reached the view. A drag passing over the top bar or the property panel stalled, and a release there left the view panning with no button held.
- Not the frame rate: every room, panning, with vsync off, averages 0.6-1.9 ms a frame (p95 under 4 ms, i.e. 270+ FPS), in Talos and alone. (The Library isn't in the FPS tour.)

Done:
- editor_screen.gd: the host takes no mouse (MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE); its tools' own Controls still take theirs.
- zoo.gd: a drag starts on the view (as before) and remembers its button. It is then followed in _input, before the interface: motion pans 1:1 wherever the mouse goes, and that button's release ends it anywhere. A motion without the button held also ends it (a release lost outside the window).

Tests: test_editor.test_library_drag_pans_in_talos (in Talos: the host takes no mouse; a 540 px drag across the top bar pans 540 px; a release over the bar ends it; a motion with no button ends it). It fails without the fix. 246 pass.

Files: scripts/editor_screen.gd, scripts/zoo.gd, tests/test_editor.gd.

## 2026-11-14 - Ships worth buying: stats by class and grade, prices from what they give
Asked: "ship prices are also too low and they don't offer much of an upgrade in hull, shields etc." Measured: every ship of a class had the same stats whatever it cost (every fighter 96 hull / 64 shields; the price was the only difference). The starting Atrapos (100 / 100, slots 3 / 3 / 2) beat every fighter, interceptor and courier for sale. Prices ran 4,200-11,500, while a few hours in you have 18-25k.

Done (Shipyard.stats):
- CLASS_BASE: each class's cheapest design already beats the Atrapos where the class is strong. Interceptor 110 / 100 / speed 520; fighter 150 / 130 / 460; courier 140 / 130 / 490; explorer 210 / 210 / 400; gunship 360 / 260 / 320; freighter 380 / 160 / 250; frigate 600 / 420 / 240.
- Grade: a design's place among its class's designs by listed price (0 = cheapest, 1 = dearest). Hull and shields grow up to x1.5 (GRADE_HULL), speed up to x1.12. The top third gets one more internal slot.
- Slots: no class below the Atrapos where it counts. Interceptor 2/3/2, fighter 3/3/2, courier 2/4/2, explorer 2/5/3, gunship 4/4/3, freighter 2/7/2, frigate 5/6/3.
- EMPIRE_TASTE: Sparta and Mycenae build tougher hulls (x1.15 / x1.1), Athens stronger shields (x1.12), Ionia and the Cyclades faster ships (x1.06).
- price_of: the price comes from what a ship gives - hull, shields (x1.2), slots (2,500 a hardpoint, 1,500 an internal or utility slot), hold and speed over 400 - times 0.6, so a dearer ship is always a real upgrade. The Atrapos is listed at 15,100 (its trade-in still counts the 2,500 it's worth at the start).
- Numbers: interceptors 15,500-20,500 (up to 165 / 153, speed 600); fighters 17,900-23,700 (up to 225 / 212); couriers 17,800-23,600; explorers 22,500-30,000; freighters 28,400-36,000; gunships 29,000-39,300 (up to 602 / 437); frigates 43,900-59,000 (up to 1,000 hull, 579 shields, 5 / 7 / 3).
- Ships already bought keep the value paid for them (the trade-in: 80% of it).

Tests: test_ships.test_ships_are_upgrades (every ship more hull and shields than the Atrapos, no fewer slots, priced from 15,000; each class's dearest at least x1.35 its cheapest; a frigate over twice a fighter's price and four times the Atrapos's hull).

Files: scripts/shipyard.gd, tests/test_ships.gd.

## 2026-11-14 - Ships: the best cost millions; prices on a steep curve
Asked (while the above was being done): "top ships should be 1 million credits minimum", then "adjust the rest of the ships appropriately". The straight-line price (above) is replaced: Shipyard.value() sums what a ship gives (hull, shields x1.2, slots, hold, speed over 400), and price_of() bends it - MIN_PRICE (15,000) for the weakest design, TOP_PRICE (3,000,000) for the strongest, value ^ power between (power ~3.2, calibrated from every design). The stats spread wider to match: a class's dearest design has 2x the hull and shields of its cheapest (GRADE_HULL, was 1.5) and x1.15 the speed; frigates' base 700 / 480.
Numbers: interceptors 15,000-56,400 (110/100 to 220/200); fighters 23,700-96,000 (to 300/260); couriers 23,500-93,700; explorers 49,600-220,000 (to 420/420); freighters 105,000-390,000; gunships 115,000-570,000 (to 720/582); frigates 575,000-3,000,000 (to 1,529 hull, 866 shields). Over a million: the Spartan Thermopylae (3,000,000) and Lykourgos, the Athenian Pentathlon, the Ionian Miletos, the Cycladic Sanctuary, and three Sea Peoples frigates (not sold). The Atrapos lists at 13,700.
Tests: test_ships.test_ships_are_upgrades also checks the best cost a million or more.

Items.ITEMS = the base items merged with them (Items.BASE_ITEMS).

The economy (galaxy.gd):
- Each category is made by one or two economies and used by others (a new good: by two of its category's users, picked by its name). A station deals in the original fourteen and the new goods its economy makes or uses: 40-80 kinds, ~59 on average (all 140 everywhere would have cost ~5x the economy's time). A station also buys any good you bring (it joins its market). _plan_goods works out the rates for this galaxy from how many stations of each kind it has: each good's users together use 80% of what its makers make (cheap goods flow faster); _stock_goods stocks a station's goods - at a new game, and when an older save loads (its stations get the new goods). Galaxy.makes / uses answer for both tables (the market's MADE HERE, demand bars, traders' supply premium).
- Traders plan runs over the goods both stations deal in.

Frame rate (measured in a window, 177 stations):
- cache_prices in one pass with the per-station factors worked out once, and the tick reuses the cached prices for its trend (it used to price every good again): a station's update 197 us with ~59 goods (was 154 us with 14) -> ECO_PER_FRAME 3 -> 2: ~0.48 ms a frame (was 0.46).
- The galactic averages: running totals updated as each station's prices are cached (Galaxy.sell_sum / sell_n, average_sell) instead of adding up every station's goods once a second - 11.6 ms -> 0.05 ms.
- The galaxy map's trade runs (TradeRoutes.galaxy_routes) with every market known: 62-70 ms - now a job in steps (~1 ms a frame, finishing in ~75 frames; galaxy_routes_spread for the map, which shows the last finished runs meanwhile; galaxy_routes still finishes at once for anything that needs it now). It only looks for the goods a system has to sell.

The market page: a tab per category, two rows of five, each with how many of its goods this station deals in; the table shows that category's goods; W/S step within it.

Docs: game.md (the market's 140 goods; Outfitting's tabs and before/after; the Shipyard's classes and prices).
Tests: tests/test_trade_goods.gd (new: 140 goods in 10 x 14, every good an item, the icons draw in 21 shapes; stations stock their economy's goods, every good made and used somewhere, an old save gains them; 200 ticks - no negative or NaN stock, the new goods' stocks spread out, the kept averages are the real ones; the spread route search gives the same runs). test_galaxy.test_economy_stays_supplied counts each station's own goods. test_menus_fit: every market category at 100 / 130 / 150%.

## 2026-11-14 - Missions pay by difficulty, up to ten times as much
Asked: "raise missions to pay 10 times as much", then "sorry i meant up to 10 times as much, the mission difficulty should dictate the reward". Missions.pay_mult(m) = 1 + 9 x difficulty; difficulty (0..1) = 0.6 x its tier (Routine 0 ... Hero 1) + 0.4 x its kind's danger (DANGER: courier, survey 0; supply, salvage, repair 0.3; bounty, join, defend 0.7; hunt, protect, strike, attack_fleet 1). A Routine courier run pays as before; a Hero-tier hunt, strike or raid ten times. Applied once as a job is made (_paid: offers, crisis jobs, the offer replacing one you take) and to the jobs in an older save as it loads ("pay_raised" kept in the save, so never twice). Each kind's own sizing (enemy count and hull, distance, goods' value) and the tier's pay stay. Sampled: Routine courier ~540 dr, Routine bounty ~2,600, Trusted bounty ~7,000, Honoured bounty ~22,000, Hero bounty 29,000-61,000, Hero supply up to 70,000.
Docs: game.md (Missions: pay follows difficulty). Tests: test_play.test_missions (offers raised; a Routine courier x1, a Hero hunt x10; fights pay more than deliveries, higher tiers more; an older save's job raised once). 256 pass.
Files: scripts/missions.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_play.gd.

## 2026-11-14 - Live updates always on: hot reload, screens rebuilt, a restart where you were when needed
Asked: "why my game does not update live to the latest change, i want live coding to be always on and update automatically". The running game had tried: its watcher saw the changes, but every reload failed - the new RichField class can't be registered in a running game (Godot names classes as it starts), so the scripts using it didn't compile there and kept their old code; and a screen already built (the Lore page) keeps what it built.

Done (scripts/live_link.gd):
- Always on: live updates run in every windowed debug run from the project - not exports, not headless (the tests); the user arg --no-live turns them off. --live[=PORT] still opens the port for tools/live.py.
- The watcher on a thread of its own: a pass every 0.5 s over the scripts, shaders, pictures, data and tile sheets; the main thread only reloads what it found. (Measured: file checks on the main thread blocked up to 126 ms now and then - the project is in a synced folder; now 0.006 ms a frame on average, 0.1 ms at worst.)
- After a hot reload, the screens on show rebuild with the new code (the data editor's page, the station menu, the Scenario Editor, the Ship / Field Computer's tab, Versions' entry).
- Data files the game reads itself reload too (main_quest.json, scenarios.json, themes.json) - not while Talos is open (it edits them, and a reload would drop unsaved edits).
- A change hot reload can't take - a new class_name, a script losing variables (renamed / removed: that once crashed the game), live_link.gd itself - restarts the game where you were: after 2.5 s with no more changes, on a thread (the game runs on), `godot --import` (so the new game knows the new classes) and tools/live_check.gd (new: every script compiles, in a fresh process) - never restarting into code that doesn't compile ("not restarting yet - doesn't compile: x.gd"). Then the game is saved (a slot of its own, SaveGame.LIVE - never in the lists) or Talos's tool and page noted (Talos with unsaved edits: it waits, and asks for Ctrl+S), and it restarts with the exact command line it was started with (/proc/self/cmdline) - back in space or on the planet where you were (the loading screen: "Back to the game - updated"), or the same Talos tool.
- A note in the bottom-right corner for a few seconds: "Live update: station_menu.gd", "Live: restarting to apply a new class...", "Live: not applied - doesn't compile yet: ..." (red, 6 s).
Checked in a window: a new class script -> restart -> back in space, the ship on the same spot, the window where it was, one process; touching station_menu.gd with the station menu open rebuilt it.

Also found while measuring:
- Traders' trip planning priced every good at every station in reach with a full price() each time - up to 14 ms for one departure with ~60 goods a station. It reads the price cache now (kept every economy tick): 2.4 ms at worst.
- Galaxy saves keep a trader's countdown to the millisecond: one just under zero came back from the JSON a hair off (test_galaxy.test_save_round_trip).

Tests: tests/test_live.gd (new: a new class_name needs a restart, a known one doesn't; a renamed variable does, an added one doesn't, broken code isn't a reason; the compile check catches a broken script; live updates off headless; the restart's save apart from the lists). 249 pass.

## 2026-11-14 - Nav beacon trails: fading out properly, 6 times slower, fewer at once
Asked: "the foam disappears suddenly instead of fading out, also too many overlapping foams, slow down the animation 6 times and make sure everything fades out properly".
- The sudden end: the trail shader read the wave's age from COLOR in fragment() - that's the vertex colour times the texture's (the noise the quads are drawn with so their UVs count), so the age came out scrambled by the noise and patches jumped past their end. It's read in vertex() now (a varying), as it was given: every part fades to nothing over its time.
- And it thins out toward the end of its way (it was cut off flat there).
- 6 times slower (NavBeacon.SLOW): a wave goes out over 9 s, its nebula lingers 15.6 s, the gas drifts and shimmers 6 times slower; one wave every 11 s, so about two trails at a time (were four or five). The ring keeps its pace.
Also: a Plasma Bouncer's bolt whose shooter was gone (a jump, a death) errored looking for its next target - it stops bouncing now.
Files: shaders/nav_trail.gdshader, scripts/nav_beacon.gd, scripts/plasma_bouncer.gd.

## 2026-11-14 - The Ship / Field Computer open and close with a hexagon curtain
Asked: "i want the tab menu to appear with a nice curtain animation made of hexagon tiles that grow and reveal the full gui", then "the reverse should happen when i close the tab menu".
- Opening (Tab, I, M, G - and the Field Computer on foot): a grid of hexagon tiles (radius 56 px) grows from nothing - the middle ones first, then outward to both sides like curtains drawn apart (0.36 s across, each tile up to 0.08 s at random), each tile opening in 0.26 s (eased) with its rim glowing in the theme's colour and a faint flash; the menu shows only where tiles have opened, the game behind through the rest. 0.7 s in all.
- Closing: the same backwards, 1.4 times quicker (0.5 s) - the edge tiles first, the middle last - then the menu hides; clicks don't reach it meanwhile; Tab again while it closes turns it round where it is.
- How (HexReveal, new; shaders/hex_reveal.gdshader, new): while it plays, the menu's material is the curtain shader and every part of the menu uses it (use_parent_material): each pixel works out its tile (the hex grid, the tile's delay and how far it's opened) and shows only if it's open. Done, every part gets its own look back - an open menu costs nothing more. Two ways that didn't work: clipping the menu to tiles drawn as a mask (clip_children: Godot left the menu unclipped, then drew the mask's colour over its scroll areas), and covering the closed tiles with a copy of the screen from before the menu (a screen-reading shader takes its own copy, menu included).
- Headless (the tests) menus open and close at once, as before.
Tests: test_play.test_hex_curtain (headless: closing hides at once; playing: the menu's parts use the curtain's shader; done: their own look back).

  the trail's max length per second - far quicker than the ship, a jet - at 60-100% by thrust), then slows
  to rest (DRAG 5/s), settling along the path behind.
- The fresh exhaust (its first ATTACH = 0.25 s) is drawn as a flame fixed to the nozzle: straight out
  behind it at each puff's own distance, easing into where it has really drifted - so the trail always
  leaves the nozzle along the flame, then bends away (the ship's velocity changes fast in a turn: real
  drift alone left it ~30 degrees off).
- Turning, the ship throttles right back: the exhaust's strength now follows the square root of thrust,
  so the fresh jet still shows instead of only the one from before the turn.
- The trail is capped at max_len from the nozzle in a straight line (measured along it, a spin's spray
  zigzagged and was cut off early).
Checked in a window: full speed (420 px/s), then a hard 90-degree turn, screenshots every 0.25 s.

## 2026-11-17 - 240 FPS with another game running alongside

Asked: "optimise code make sure everything runs at 240 FPS" - "i dont care if another game runs, i want
you achieve 240 FPS regardless". With a heavy game sharing the machine (its GPU at ~90%, five CPU cores
busy), 25 of 92 FPS-tour scenarios fell under 240 (the surfaces down to 175-300 fps, a signal site 87).
What every frame did was cut, so there's headroom left when the machine is shared:
- The galaxy's background traders (110, flying their routes abstractly): a quarter of them a frame, round
  robin, each moved by the time since its own last turn - every one every frame was the costliest script
  of all (0.3-0.5 ms a frame, everywhere); now ~0.04 ms.
- Surface animals off screen think every 8 frames (was 4), far ones (beyond 1500 px) every 16 (was 8) -
  the same behaviour with the time in between; ~110 animals were 0.5-1.2 ms a frame on Thalassa.
- Teleport gates redraw their glow only near the screen (UI.near_view: a thing within 300 px of the
  view) - every gate on the planet redrew it 60 times a second.
- The tentacled space monster's eight tentacles: two tapered triangle strips each (edge and body, plus a
  thin anti-aliased outline) instead of 34 anti-aliased line segments - ~1 ms a redraw, every 4th frame
  (the monsters room in Talos missed its p95). Looks the same, without the seams between segments.
- Enemy ships keeping apart: their positions and sizes gathered once a frame into packed arrays and far
  ones skipped at once - all pairs with node lookups each was 0.3 ms with 40 ships (Kyros).
- A fight's first explosion: 27 ms (a hitch) - its sounds read from disk, the wreck shader and the
  explosion's particle blend made right then. Now on entering space every space sound is loaded in the
  background (Sfx.warm: one a frame) and an explosion, a shockwave and a wreck are drawn once unseen
  (Effects.warm, Wreck.warm). The battle's worst frame: 28.6 -> 10.9 ms.
- Quest scenarios' state-like conditions (near a place, has an item) checked 20 times a second (or every
  4th frame, if sooner) instead of every frame (~0.2 ms); timers and "every N seconds" still each frame.
- The exhaust's lightning streaks use every other point of the trail (the costliest drawing in a battle:
  ~0.26 ms a frame for its glow) - they look as jagged.
- (Second round, during a heavy match of the other game.) The radar's asteroid dots: one batch of small
  octagons (a triangle array) instead of a draw_circle each - a ring site's hundreds of rocks made each
  radar redraw ~1 ms (30 a second); the ring site 140 -> 261 fps.
- Surface animals re-check that the straight way to where they're going is open once a second (was every
  half second: ~0.45 ms a frame among Thalassa's ~100 animals).
- A trader's catch-up is capped at 10 s (time since its last turn).
- Doc pictures: the space HUD's "Your objective" note points at the quest text again, the nav beacon's
  "On the radar too" at the beacon on the radar (both moved with the smaller minimap).
- (Third round - measured by switching parts of a running surface off: its processing was ~1 ms of a
  ~1.9 ms frame, all the scenery's drawing ~0.35 ms - so processing, not baking the scenery into
  pictures, was where the time was.) Surface animals off the screen now sleep: no _process of their own;
  the surface wakes an eighth of its sleepers each frame (far ones every other turn) to think with the
  time they slept, and one comes back to every-frame thinking in view, fighting or hit. On Thalassa ~74 of
  ~92 animals sleep at a time (each one's own _process, even returning at once, was ~4 us a frame).
- A bug: an animal walking a clear way re-checked that the way was clear every frame (the check's
  target was the route planner's, only set when routing) - ~0.35 ms a frame; now once a second (4 times
  a second chasing or fleeing).
- The surface's own frame: lifting what stands on the ground skips what hasn't moved (its drawn transform
  keeps the lift; all re-lifted every 30 frames), the health bar is updated only when your health changes
  (setting its colour redrew it every frame), and the building / villager / gate plans are looked

## 2026-11-19 - Damaged parts and the Repair Bay (surgery on your ship and automaton)

Asked: complex damage to the different parts of the ship and the automaton, a GUI to go in and fix them
part by part, a specialised scanner to find the faults and spare parts to replace damaged parts - like
a surgical operation, with complex mechanics and interesting interactions.
Done:
- Parts (scripts/parts.gd): the ship has 8 parts (Sensor Array, Weapon Mounts, Reactor Core, Shield
  Emitter, Manoeuvring Thrusters, Main Engines, Fuel Lines, Hull Plating), the automaton 6 (Optic Head,
  Power Core, Arm Actuators, Heat Sinks, Leg Servos, Chassis Frame), each of 3-5 components (circuit,
  conduit, servo, plate, lens, cell). Hull damage (and the automaton's on foot) can leave a fault -
  chance 4 x the hit's share of max health, max 85%; the side it came from picks the part (engines and
  fuel lines from behind, sensors ahead); the damage type its kind (lasers burn wiring, heat leaks).
  5 kinds: crack, burnt wiring, leak, misalignment, wrecked component; the same fault hit again worsens,
  beaten past repair it becomes a wreck. Up to 5 a part.
- What faults do: each part loses its share of an effect (speed -45% engines, handling -55% thrusters,
  shield recharge -80% reactor, max shields -55% emitter, fire rate / damage weapons, range sensors,
  fuel leaking from the lines, +60% hull damage taken through the plating; the automaton: reach, rate
  of fire, walking speed, healing and health, damage taken). PlayerData.mod adds the ship's;
  Pilot.apply_gear the automaton's. Saved with the player ("condition").
- The Repair Bay (scripts/repair_bay.gd, RepairArt drawings in scripts/repair_art.gd): a new REPAIR tab
  in the Ship Computer (8 tabs) and the Field Computer. Schematic (the ship's own picture behind its
  parts) and part list; the operating table; vitals (a pulse racing with the heat, temperature,
  pressure, how well it works, power); the breaker; 7 tools; 4 scan modes; spare parts; faults found.
  Surgery: undo 6 bolts (neighbours in a row strain the casing - it warps and cracks a component);
  scan (each fault kind in its mode; the built-in scanner has Structure and Thermal, the Mk II adds
  Field and Resonance, the Mk III reads through the closed casing); weld a crack by tracing it slowly
  (too fast: no bead; resting: burns through); solder burnt wiring strand by strand to matching colours
  (power on: a shock, heat and maybe more burnt wiring; wrong terminal: a short); seal a leak only at low
  pressure (a gauge; at high pressure it's blown off); calibrate frequency and phase with two dials onto
  a reference wave; replace a wreck (clamps, drag it out, take a spare, turn it to the socket's notch,
  seat it, clamps shut). Heat past 100 scorches a component (a new fault); an open part with a live leak
  vents and heats. The automaton's power core can't be cut.
- Items: 6 spare parts (40-90 dr) and the Diagnostic Scanner Mk II (650) and Deep Scanner Mk III (1500),
  sold with the stations' supplies; wrecks drop a spare 40% of the time (stations 1-3).
- Stations' Repair tab: the technicians fix all of a body's faults (60 + 140 x severity a fault, +220 a
  wreck).
- Pilot's guide: new section "The Repair Bay" (repair-bay) + doc shot repair_bay.
- Tests: tests/test_repair.gd (4 tests: hits and effects, the ship and automaton feeling them, a full
  surgery by mouse events through every tool, careless surgery's consequences).

## 2026-11-19 - Repair Bay: a fault that changes kind under your hands

Found by a flaky test (test_repair.test_surgery_on_the_engines, about one run in three under load):
the shock from soldering a live cable adds a "burn" complication on a random component - sometimes the
very cable being soldered, which made it worse and could turn it into a wreck (same fault id). The table
then kept the cable's soldering state for what was now a wreck (no "stage": script errors on every
forceps click, the part couldn't be fixed). Two fixes in scripts/repair_bay.gd:
- Table.fstate remembers the kind a fault's work state was made for, and makes it anew when the fault
  changed kind (a burn beaten past repair is a wreck: clamps, lift, seat).
- complication() lands on a component without that fault (or a wreck) when there is one - a new fault,
  as the log says ("New fault: ..."), not the one under your hands made worse; only when every component
  has one already does it make one worse.

## 2026-11-19 - Repair Bay: no new faults from working on a part

Asked: undoing the casing's bolts produced a new affliction - afflictions should come only from damage to the
hull (or the automaton's body).

only logs). Each costs work instead:
